hx_detect_edge_segments — 2D halcon_ext op

• Data kinds: image → region

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "hx_detect_edge_segments", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Detect straight edge fragments: thin by NMS, then keep the connected components that PCA finds elongated (line-like).

Splits the edges thinned by hx_nonmax_dir(v, a, 0) (> 0) into connected components with the 8-neighbourhood, and returns a 0/1 float region in which only components whose covariance eigenvalue ratio of pixel coordinates λmax/λmin is at least min_ratio (elongated = line-like) are 1.

• a → weak-edge threshold of the thinning stage (same as a of hx_nonmax_dir; normalised amplitudes below a*0.3 are discarded).

• b → elongation threshold min_ratio = 3 + b*12 (3 to 15). The larger, the more only straight fragments remain.

• Components with fewer than 5 pixels are discarded unconditionally. If λmin is nearly 0 (a perfect line), the ratio is taken as infinite and the component is adopted.

Caution: the linearity test is "whether the spread of the point cloud is biased toward 1 axis", so even curves pass if they are elongated enough. Because the thinning stage hardly thins diagonal edges (see the notes of hx_nonmax_dir), diagonal edges become thick blobs whose eigenvalue ratio drops, and they tend to be dropped. Since it works per connected component, crossing lines form 1 component and the ratio drops. To handle each line segment downstream, use hx_region_to_label or hough_line_trans.

Blank frame (measured): feeding an image of uniform brightness gives an empty result — every pixel is background (0) — regardless of the brightness. Pure white and pure black behave alike; brightness by itself detects nothing.
